liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): Reviewer felt the band played this opener at too fast a tempo [25]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer calls Let It Grow phenomenal, along with Black Peter, and praises Not Fade Away and Throwing Stones [35]
- **In The Midnight Hour** (1 review): Reviewer calls this Midnight Hour magical [33]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Playin' in the Band into Terrapin is described as very smooth, familiar from the 'So Far' video [27]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Commenter notes Black Peter appearing late in the second set is an unusual placement [34]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): Reviewer likes the tone of this version and Bobby's treatment of the lyrics, with a weary feel at the end [31]

## The recordings

- **gd85-12-31.aud.barbella.12086.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 170 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording described as soundboard-like in quality, with loud, clear crowd and band; called the best of three sources [32]
- **gd1985-12-31.178209.neumann.blend.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 27 songs; 160 min [2]
- **gd1985-12-31.142017.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 182 min [5]
- **gd85-12-31.sbd.prefm.ashley-bertha.20006.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 24 songs; 147 min; rated 3.79/5 by 24 [19]. Said about its sound: Reviewer complains that Jerry's vocals are very low in the mix on this version [30]

## Around the show

- Parking-lot fliers urged fans to clap and stomp Not Fade Away as the band walked on, to sway the opening choice [26]
- Broadcast on USA Network from intermission; Ken Kesey animatedly described the giant birthday cake float rolling across the floor before midnight [28]
- Fliers outside worked: the band responded to the crowd's request; crowd energy was great, though band seemed ragged by year's end [31]
- Baba Olatunji played percussion on the Throwing Stones, Not Fade Away, Love Light sequence [2]
- Reviewer found it an average show, below the level of most of 1985 [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-12-31.aud.barbella.12086.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>?>DAT>CDR [1]. Also: Audience source via DAT to CDR; encore taken from Peter Braverman's Nak 300 cassette master; seeded to etree by Steve Barbella [1]
- **gd1985-12-31.178209.neumann.blend.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; 3 x Neumann mic blend (unknown model)> unknown mixer > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell UDXLII 90) [2]. Also: Source cassettes and transfer by Scott Wiseman; Charlie Miller coordinated; Sennheiser 421 source patches gaps in Terrapin, Drums/Space, and Black Peter transitions [2]
- **gd1985-12-31.142017.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: transferred by 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound Mix (48k) by Kevin Tobin; source: flac16/48kHz; 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound (48k) - SBD (shnid = 106021) Recording Info: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/Maxell MX-90); Transfer Info: Cassette… [5]. Also: A 5.1 surround mix of the show was made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in 2018 [5]
- **gd85-12-31.sbd.prefm.ashley-bertha.20006.sbeok.shnf**: source: Bertha Remaster of the PreFM Soundboard source. SBD(PreFM)>>CASS>>DAT>>CDA>>DAW(Bertha)>>CDA/SHN by Jay Ashley [19]. Also: Reviewer taped it from radio broadcast, later also saw it on USA Network; their tape's first set was lost [35]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Arena - December 31, 1985](https://www.dead.net/show/december-31-1985) [38]
- Fan art by www.walmart.com: [Robot or human?](https://www.walmart.com/ip/Oakland-Coliseum-Arena-Oakland-CA-31st-Dec-1985-The-Grateful-Dead-CD/1481180514) [39]
- Poster by Brian Baumwoll Grateful Dead: [1985-12-30 Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum, Oakland, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1985-12-30-oakland-alameda-county-coliseum-oakland-ca-usa/) [40]

claims.text: Reviewer felt the band played this opener at too fast a tempo
Parking-lot fliers urged fans to clap and stomp Not Fade Away as the band walked on, to sway the opening choice
Playin' in the Band into Terrapin is described as very smooth, familiar from the 'So Far' video
Broadcast on USA Network from intermission; Ken Kesey animatedly described the giant birthday cake float rolling across the floor before midnight
Reviewer found it an average show, below the level of most of 1985
Reviewer complains that Jerry's vocals are very low in the mix on this version
Fliers outside worked: the band responded to the crowd's request; crowd energy was great, though band seemed ragged by year's end
Reviewer likes the tone of this version and Bobby's treatment of the lyrics, with a weary feel at the end
Audience recording described as soundboard-like in quality, with loud, clear crowd and band; called the best of three sources
Reviewer calls this Midnight Hour magical
Commenter notes Black Peter appearing late in the second set is an unusual placement
Reviewer calls Let It Grow phenomenal, along with Black Peter, and praises Not Fade Away and Throwing Stones
Reviewer taped it from radio broadcast, later also saw it on USA Network; their tape's first set was lost
Audience source via DAT to CDR; encore taken from Peter Braverman's Nak 300 cassette master; seeded to etree by Steve Barbella
Source cassettes and transfer by Scott Wiseman; Charlie Miller coordinated; Sennheiser 421 source patches gaps in Terrapin, Drums/Space, and Black Peter transitions
Baba Olatunji played percussion on the Throwing Stones, Not Fade Away, Love Light sequence
A 5.1 surround mix of the show was made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in 2018
